metric_model: CHAOSS AI Alignment - Community Governed Use

scope.note: Scoring confined to the files named on the command line; 'no' means not addressed in those files.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: Applies to Pull Requests, Issues, and comments that include AI-generated code, documentation, or comments; disclosure required if AI generated 'a significant portion' (beyond simple autocomplete).
domains.accountability_holder: The human contributor ("The human contributor is the sole party responsible for the contribution.")

evidence.quote: The human contributor is the sole party responsible for the contribution.
You must fully understand every line of code in the submission.
we require you to disclose it in the Pull Request description

domains.reasoning: The policy names PRs, issues, and comments explicitly, requires the human contributor to understand and explain the code (human-in-the-loop), requires disclosure via an 'Assisted-by' trailer for significant AI use, and states the contributor is the sole responsible party. Both supervision level and accountability holder are stated, so this is fully addressed.

domains.suggested_improvement: no supervision level; no scope or accountability holder named
domains.reasoning: The policy contains no mention of meeting recording, transcription, or notetaker bots of any kind.

domains.suggested_improvement: no rule for blogs/design assets outside PR scope
domains.reasoning: The only mention of 'documentation' is within the code-contribution context ('a Pull Request that includes AI-generated code, documentation, or comments'), which is scoped to code_contributions, not to general content like blog posts or design assets. No separate content policy is stated.

domains.suggested_improvement: no supervision level; no accountability holder for moderation AI use
domains.reasoning: The policy makes no reference to moderation actions or the use of AI in moderating community spaces, issues, or the platform.

domains.suggested_improvement: no explicit rule on maintainers'/reviewers' own use of AI
domains.reasoning: The document discusses the contributor's conduct during the review process ('Copy-and-pasting to and from an AI chatbot during the process of code review is not acceptable') and implies human-only review ('Humans will take time to review the code'), but it never states a rule about whether maintainers/reviewers themselves may use AI tools to conduct review. Because this only restricts the contributor's behavior around the review process rather than naming who may review using AI, it is not addressed; the restrictive tone toward AI in the review process is recorded as a lean.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: Covers autonomous submission of Pull Requests and posting of comments on issues/PRs.
domains.accountability_holder: The human contributor (per the same Accountability section: "The human contributor is the sole party responsible for the contribution.")

evidence.quote: Autonomous AI agents may not submit Pull Requests to Mastodon repositories.
Do not post comments on issues or PRs that are AI-generated. Discussions on the Mastodon repositories are for humans only.

domains.reasoning: The policy explicitly bans autonomous AI agents from submitting PRs and bans AI-generated comments on issues/PRs, stating discussions are 'for humans only.' This is a clear supervision level (banned). Accountability is drawn from the same section's general statement that the human contributor is the sole responsible party for any contribution, which the autonomous-agent ban immediately follows.

The policy's stated rationale is about maintainer overhead, code quality, and authentic human connection; it never raises energy, water, or carbon footprint concerns, so there is no lean or rule to record.

domains.rationale_only_mention: These latter forms of AI assistance cause major overhead for project maintainers. There are a small number of people on the Mastodon core team, and we seek to use our time and resources effectively.
domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on server load or hardware/financing strain
domains.reasoning: The policy cites maintainer time/effort overhead as a reason to discourage AI contributions, but this is about human reviewer bandwidth, not server load or hardware cost/financing (infrastructure as defined). No rule on infrastructure strain is set; the concern is recorded as a rationale-only mention with a restrictive lean toward AI generally.

domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on use of platform/user data for AI training
domains.reasoning: The Copyright & Legal section addresses provenance and licensing of AI-generated code output (e.g., not violating AI provider ToS or including regurgitated code), but this concerns the legality of code the contributor submits, not the use of Mastodon platform/user data to train AI models. No mention of training data use is made.

consent_policy_specificity.overall_posture: The policy is highly specific about code contributions - requiring human accountability, disclosure, and banning autonomous PR/comment submission - but is entirely silent on notetaker bots, general content, moderation, reviewer-side AI use, environmental impact, infrastructure strain, and training data use, and only reaches those areas of general concern (maintainer overhead) as rationale rather than rule.

validation_problems: code_contributions: quote not found in AI_POLICY.md

awaiting_implementation.specific_tools_in_use: Awaiting implementation: named-product detection beyond known file signatures
awaiting_implementation.ai_tool_owner: Awaiting implementation: ownership and data control
awaiting_implementation.environmental_footprint: Awaiting implementation: model/system card and ESG disclosure
awaiting_implementation.proportionality: Awaiting implementation: resource use relative to contributor count (needs platform usage data)

use_composition_partial.note: Detection only. Absence of signal is not absence of use.

policy_change.blocker: Draft classifier not wired in or validated against hand-graded history. Repo.history() and Repo.commit_patch() supply the diffs.

use_compliance.blocker: Derived metric. Requires disclosed-use data (Use Composition) checked against the specificity grid. Composition is only partially detectable, so the comparison is not yet sound.

misuse.blocker: Not automatable. CHAOSS marks the core signals unknown: text-based AI detectors are unreliable, and license-laundering and wrongful-accusation incidents need maintainer self-report.
